svg.text: How a node's figures reach the command line — and where a lane that cannot carry them refuses
One entry point, two outcomes: the figure is attached at the launcher, resolved through the lane's command, and either emitted as image flags or refused by the lane's own name.
node declares figures
the images the run wrote
images=("a.png","b.png")
launch_plan(..., images=...)
the plan the launcher runs —
the test reads .argv, not a helper
dialect selected by command
keyed on the command's own name — the
configured lane, not the model behind it
dialect.argv(images)
codex declares image
no image flag
codex exec — one flag per file
each -i is immediately followed by its own
path, and precedes the resume subcommand:
codex exec --json -C /wt ...
-i a.png -i b.png -
images=() emits no -i; the flag carries the
attachment, so the path is where it lands.
claude · clive · in-harness
raises BackendError naming the lane; it never
drops the figure and answers without the image:
the 'clive' dialect cannot carry
attached images, so 1 figure(s)
A figureless node on the same lane is
unaffected: the refusal responds to the figure.
The refusal is the measure. A lane that answers from the filename, the path and the diff returns a well-formed verdict it could not have formed.
